input: Research noise-canceling headphones within my budget

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The budget ceiling defines which products are even eligible — a $50 limit leads to a completely different set of recommendations than a $300 limit.
Noise-canceling headphones span over-ear, on-ear, and in-ear (earbuds) form factors with very different ANC performance, comfort, and portability trade-offs.
The primary use environment — commuting, office, travel, gym, home — determines which ANC strength, durability, and feature set matters most.
Whether this is for the user personally or as a gift affects whose preferences, head size, hearing needs, and device ecosystem should drive the choice.
Priorities like sound quality, battery life, microphone quality, or comfort weight the comparison differently and narrow the shortlist significantly.
Knowing what a successful research output looks like — a ranked shortlist, a single final pick, a comparison table — determines how deep and structured the research needs to be.
Where the user plans to buy (online retailer, local store, specific platform) and whether they need the headphones by a certain date affects which options are actually available to them.

gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate noise-canceling headphone options that fit the user's budget and needs.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for the headphones?
questions.description: Establish the hard spending ceiling to filter eligible products.

questions.title: Which form factor do you prefer: over-ear, on-ear, or earbuds?
questions.description: Identify the physical style of headphone to narrow the product category.

questions.title: Where will you use these headphones most — commuting, office, travel, or home?
questions.description: Pinpoint the primary use environment to match ANC strength and durability needs.

questions.title: Are you buying these for yourself or as a gift for someone?
questions.description: Determine whose preferences, device ecosystem, and physical fit should guide the research.

questions.title: What feature matters most to you: sound quality, battery life, mic quality, or comfort?
questions.description: Surface the single top priority to weight the comparison criteria correctly.

questions.title: Do you want a shortlist of options or one final recommendation?
questions.description: Define the expected output format so the research depth and structure is appropriate.

questions.title: Where do you plan to purchase — online, a specific store, or no preference?
questions.description: Identify the buying channel and any deadline to ensure recommended products are actually accessible.
